title: HILIC-MS Analysis of Central Carbon Metabolites in Gram Negative Bacteria
author: Bashar Amer
materials: Calibration curves: Pure analytical standards were dissolved in 50:50 methanol:water (v/v) to make a stock solution of 100 micromolar (µM) concentration. The stock solution was diluted 4-fold to make a standard solution of 25 micromolar (µM) (with 50:50 methanol:water, v/v). A seven-point calibration curve was produced via a series of 2-fold serial dilutions (with 50:50 methanol:water, v/v), which were conducted from the 25 micromolar (µM) standard solution to a standard solution ending in a concentration of 0.390625 micromolar (µM) ; 2-fold serial dilutions for CoA standards, however, were conducted from a 20 micromolar (µM) standard solution to standard solution ending in a concentration of 0.3125 micromolar (µM) . All solutions were prepared on ice and stored at -20 °C until LC-MS data acquisition. Extraction of intracellular metabolites: Wild type Escherichia coli DH1 ( E. coli ) and Pseudomonas putida K2440 ( P. putida) were grown on 0.5% glucose in LB medium at 37 °C . Growth was monitored during mid exponential phase to early stationary phase. E. coli and P. putida reached average optical densities at 600 nm wavelength (OD 600 nm) of 1.67 and 2.16, respectively. 1.5 mL of the cell culture was harvested (in triplicate) and transferred to a 2 mL centrifuge tube. The cell culture was centrifuged at 14000 x g, °C, for 2 minutes at room temperature. After removing the supernatant, metabolic activity from the cell pellet was quenched by adding 250 µL of ice-cold methanol and mixing thoroughly by vortexing for 2 minutes at 4 °C . 250 µL of water was then added to the methanol lysate, mixed by vortexing, and centrifuged at 14000 x g, °C, for 5 minutes at 4 °C . 450 µL rpm, °C, of the lysate was filtered via a 3k Da molecular weight cut-off centrifuge filter (Amicon-Ultra, part number UFC500396, MilliPoreSigma, St. Louis, MO, USA) at 13000 x g, °C, at 4 °C , for 60 minutes prior to LC-MS analysis. Liquid Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry Analysis of Isoprenoid Intermediates in Escherichia coli.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.).

steps.title: Prepare mobile phases A and B
steps.instruction: Make mobile phase A containing 10 mM ammonium acetate, 0.2 % (v/v) ammonium hydroxide and 5 µM medronic acid in water; make mobile phase B with the same reagents in 90 % (v/v) acetonitrile (water makes up the remaining 10 %).

steps.title: Degas and pre‑purge UHPLC pump
steps.instruction: Sonicate both mobile phases for 5 min, then purge the 1290 Infinity II UHPLC pump with a 1:1 mixture of A and B for up to 5 min before installing the column.

steps.title: Install and equilibrate HILIC column
steps.instruction: Mount an Agilent InfinityLab Poroshell 120 HILIC‑Z column (2.1 mm ID × 100 mm, 2.7 µm particles) with its matching guard column (2.1 mm ID, 2.7 µm). Set the column compartment to 30 °C and the sample tray to 5 °C. Equilibrate the column with the starting mobile‑phase composition at 0.1 mL min⁻¹ until the back‑pressure stabilises (maximum 600 bar).

steps.title: Set injection volume and temperatures
steps.instruction: Program the autosampler to inject 1 µL of each sample; keep the sample tray at 5 °C and the column compartment at 30 °C throughout the run.

steps.title: Program UHPLC gradient
steps.instruction: Use the following gradient (Table 2) at the indicated flow rates: 0 min – 90 % B, 0.250 mL min⁻¹; 2 min – 90 % B, 0.250 mL min⁻¹; 11.5 min – 61.5 % B, 0.250 mL min⁻¹; 11.7 min – 60 % B, 0.330 mL min⁻¹; 12.7 min – 60 % B, 0.400 mL min⁻¹; 12.9 min – 90 % B, 0.550 mL min⁻¹; 14.3 min – 90 % B, 0.550 mL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Connect UHPLC to QTOF MS and set ion source
steps.instruction: Couple the UHPLC outlet to an Agilent 6545 QTOF‑MS via the Agilent Jet Stream (AJS) ion source. Operate the source in negative ion mode to generate [M‑H]⁻ or [M‑2H]²⁻ ions.

steps.title: Prepare and deliver reference mass solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the reference ions—trifluoroacetic acid anion ([M‑H]⁻, m/z 112.98559) and HP‑0921 (hexakis(1H,1H,3H‑tetrafluoropropoxy)phosphazine, m/z 1033.98811)—to 2 µM in 80:20 acetonitrile:water (v/v). Deliver this solution to the electrospray sprayer at 5 µL min⁻¹ using the 1260 Infinity II Isocratic Pump.

steps.title: Tune QTOF MS and set acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Before analysis, tune the 6545 QTOF‑MS with the ESI‑L‑Low calibration solution for an acquisition range up to 1700 m/z. Then set the following parameters (Table 3): acquisition range 70‑1100 m/z; acquisition rate 0.86 spectra s⁻¹; nebulizer pressure 20 psi; drying gas temperature 300 °C; drying gas flow 10 L min⁻¹; sheath gas temperature 350 °C; sheath gas flow 12 L min⁻¹; capillary voltage 3500 V; fragmentor 100 V; skimmer 50 V; OCT 1 RF Vpp 300 V; nozzle voltage 2000 V.

steps.title: Acquire data with MassHunter software
steps.instruction: Run the LC‑MS sequence using Agilent MassHunter Workstation (version 8) for data acquisition.

steps.title: Process data with Qualitative Analysis and Profinder
steps.instruction: Process and analyse the acquired data using Agilent MassHunter Qualitative Analysis (version 6) and Profinder (version 8).
